items.title: Vince Lateano interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Francisco, California, August 8, 2002
items.q: lucky enough to be under the tutelage of this man, Aubrey Pennyman

ctx.x: Well I think it’s an important thing that teachers of jazz — and I suppose you could say this about anything, but especially of jazz, ought to be players first. And I’m not sure that’s the norm anymore in the universities.

Well universities I don’t know. I don’t spend much time in universities. I go in to just middle schools and high schools, and band directors at most of these places are not jazz musicians. But the high school I went to, the band director was not a jazz musician but he was a good musician and he was very open and he encouraged myself, Rufus Reid, he was a year behind me, Mel Martin — I don’t know if you talked to Mel — and a few other guys that have made a living playing music, went to this school and were lucky…
Did you choose to go in the service?
